scorecards.inningsCommentary: India commenced their first innings at Galle International Stadium, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 190 from S Dhawan, complemented by a commanding 253-run stand between Cheteshwar Pujara and S Dhawan that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 4.46 RPO. Sri Lanka's bowling response was spearheaded by N Pradeep (6/130), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 600/10 (133.1 ov), India established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Sri Lanka began their reply under scoreboard pressure, tasked with responding to India's opening innings total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 92 from MDK Perera, complemented by a commanding 62-run stand between MDK Perera and AD Mathews that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.7 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by Ravindra Jadeja (3/67), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Reaching 291/9 (78.3 ov), Sri Lanka's innings completed the first-innings exchange (309 Runs (India)), shaping the strategic contours for the second half of the Test.

scorecards.inningsCommentary: Sri Lanka embarked on a high-stakes fourth-innings chase of 550 Runs, confronting a deteriorating pitch and aggressive field settings. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 97 from FDM Karunaratne, complemented by a commanding 101-run stand between N Dickwella and FDM Karunaratne that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.17 RPO. India's bowling response was spearheaded by R Ashwin (3/65), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 245/8 (76.5 ov), Sri Lanka succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as India's bowlers closed out the victory.

Sri Lanka responded with 291/9 as both teams traded momentum in high-stakes middle sessions. A ruthless second-innings declaration at 240/3d by India established a massive 550 Runs target. India's bowling attack dismantled Sri Lanka for 245/8 in the fourth innings to complete the win.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Galle International Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as India posted 600/10 (133.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Sri Lanka countered with 291/9 (78.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: N Pradeep (6/130), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, S Dhawan delivered a masterclass for India (204 Runs), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (India 51%) and allowing India to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Sri Lanka faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. India's bowling unit, bolstered by Cheteshwar Pujara (168 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing India won by 304 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: India's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Sri Lanka produced fighting phases, India won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
